title: Claim
description: A statement the workspace currently makes about itself: a tenet, a direction, a practice, or a decision. There is no Practice object -- current practice is a projection over establishing and superseding events, and observations test it.
$comment: kind x state x provenance/authority x validity are orthogonal. `state` is the document lifecycle and says nothing about who established the claim; `established_by` is provenance and says nothing about whether the claim is operative; `validity` is the interval and says nothing about either. A claim published to kctl travels as a knowledge entry -- this schema is the shape, kctl is the store.

kind.description: Tenets, directions and practices are all claims. Observations corroborate or contradict them; none of them is a separate object.

state.description: Document lifecycle. `current` means operative, not approved.

basis_for.description: What this claim is the basis for. Presence makes it canonical, and its dependents are the realignment blast radius. Canonicality is a product-dependency relation -- never approval, maturity or permanence -- so it is never inferred from a raw dependent count.

enforcement_mode.description: The tenet/invariant distinction, and the only thing that distinguishes them. `review` (a tenet): divergence opens a realignment session. `block` (an invariant): violation stops the work.

establishedBy.description: Provenance and authority basis. Declared, not authenticated. `actor_type` records who acted; it never gates anything.
